title: Brisbane Pre-Sale Handyman Checklist: Cheap Fixes That Win Buyers
excerpt: Small defects cost Brisbane sellers big money at inspection. Here's exactly what to fix, what to skip, and how to spend wisely before listing.
body:
First impressions at a property inspection are formed fast — often within 90 seconds of a buyer walking through the gate. In Brisbane's competitive 2026 market, buyers are scrutinising every detail, and a squeaky door or peeling fence paint can plant doubt that's hard to shift. The good news: most of the fixes that matter cost under $200 each and require no tradesperson.

## Why Small Defects Carry Outsized Weight

Buyers use visible defects as bargaining chips, or worse, as reasons to walk away. A scuffed skirting board doesn't mean your home is poorly built — but it signals to buyers that maintenance may have been neglected more broadly. Real estate agents in Brisbane consistently report that well-presented properties receive faster offers and fewer price negotiations, even when the underlying property is identical to a nearby listing.

## The Exterior: Start at the Kerb

Buyers form judgments before they reach the front door. Work through the exterior systematically:

- **Gates and latches:** Lubricate hinges with a spray like WD-40 or a silicone lubricant. Replace any broken latches — hardware stores stock standard fittings for $10–$30. A gate that swings open smoothly signals a cared-for home.
- **Fences:** Tighten loose palings with a drill and exterior screws. Spot-prime and repaint peeling sections with a matching fence paint. Full repaints rarely pay off, but obvious patches do.
- **Paths and driveways:** Hire a pressure washer (around $60–$80/day from Kennards or similar) and blast away Brisbane's characteristic mould and dirt staining. This alone transforms the look of a property.
- **Rubbish and clutter:** Remove all bins, broken pots, unused tools, and stored materials from visible areas. Stack or store garden hoses neatly. Skip bins are available from around $300 if you have significant junk to move.
- **Gardens:** Mow, edge, and weed garden beds the week before every inspection. Add a fresh layer of mulch ($8–$12 per bag from Bunnings) to garden beds — it photographs beautifully and looks immediately tidy. Trim any overgrown hedges that block windows or the facade.

## Interior: Focus on What Eyes and Hands Touch

Indoors, buyers touch door handles, open cupboards, and look at ceilings. Target those contact points:

- **Doors:** Tighten loose hinges with longer screws if the existing holes are stripped. Plane or sand doors that stick — Brisbane's humidity causes timber to swell, and a dragging door is one of the most noticeable defects during an inspection walkthrough.
- **Touch-up paint:** Buy a small quantity of your existing wall colour (check tins in the garage, or take a chip to a paint shop for colour matching) and touch up scuffs, nail holes, and marks. Pay particular attention to hallways, near light switches, and around door frames where paint wears fastest.
- **Ceilings:** Small water stains from past leaks (that have since been repaired) can be spot-primed and painted over. If the leak is ongoing, fix the source first — a buyer's building inspector will find it.
- **Taps and shower heads:** Clean calcium and limescale build-up with white vinegar or a descaler. Replace washers on dripping taps (a plumber charges around $80–$150 for a straightforward washer replacement in Brisbane — worth it).
- **Cupboard doors:** Tighten or replace loose hinges and adjust doors that hang crooked. Replace missing or broken handles — matching handles are usually $5–$15 each.
- **Exhaust fans:** Clean grilles and test that fans are working. A non-functional bathroom exhaust is a minor issue that looks major.

## A Quick Priority Matrix

| Fix | Typical Cost | DIY Possible? | Buyer Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pressure wash paths/driveways | $60–$80 hire | Yes | High |
| Touch-up interior paint | $20–$60 | Yes | High |
| Lubricate/fix gate & door hardware | $10–$40 | Yes | Medium–High |
| Fresh garden mulch | $40–$80 | Yes | High |
| Dripping tap repair | $80–$150 | Usually no | Medium |
| Rubbish removal | $0–$300 | Yes | High |
| Replace broken handles/hinges | $15–$60 | Yes | Medium |

## What to Leave Alone

Not every fix is worth starting. Avoid these traps:

- **Major structural or drainage work** done purely for cosmetic appeal — buyers' building inspectors will inspect these areas anyway, and rushed work can raise more questions than it answers.
- **Full kitchen or bathroom renovations** — the ROI on a pre-sale renovation is rarely positive in a standard Brisbane home. Clean and declutter instead.
- **Repainting entire rooms** unless the colour is extremely unusual or the existing paint is in very poor condition — mismatched touch-ups can look worse than consistent wear.
- **Landscaping overhauls** — buyers discount large gardens that look high-maintenance. A neat, simple garden beats an ambitious one that looks hard to keep up.

## Your Actionable Takeaway

Book a single weekend six to eight weeks before your listing goes live. Walk the property as a buyer would — start at the kerb, move to the gate, along the path, through the front door, and into each room. Take photos of every defect on your phone. Then work through the list above in order of buyer visibility. Spend your time and money on what buyers see and touch first; everything else is secondary.

A few hundred dollars and a couple of weekends of effort can be the difference between a smooth sale at your asking price and weeks of negotiation.
author: PropertyHub Editorial
